newsitem.title: New Zealand: NZ shares end firmer but fail to hold early gains.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end firmer but fail to hold early gains.

text.p: * NZ shares end firmer but off highs
* Turnover moderate, despite Dow's huge rally overnight
* Lion Nathan gains ahead of Monday's 1st half profit result
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
130 nil * NZSE-40 cap index +3.70 at 2,254.54
311 +1 * NZSC cap index +9.07 at 4,961.33
356 +9 * Volume NZ$50.7 million. Futures untraded
656 nil * Other movers - +12 -7
New Zealand share prices closed firmer on Wednesday but failed to hold gains made early in the session on the back of Wall Street's substantial rally overnight.
"It wasn't a particularly sexy market. Most stocks ran up four or five cents on the opening but they've all ended up back where they started by the close," said Sean Vaughan at County Natwest.
The NZSE-40 Capital index closed 3.70 points firmer at 2,254.54, but down from its intraday high of 2,264.20.
The standout stock on the day was Lion Nathan, which rose nine cents to $3.56.
Brokers said investors were reluctant to sell any Lion stock leading into the company's first half profit result on Monday.
Analysts expect the Australasian beer and beverage brewer to report a net profit of between NZ$67-69 million for the six month to February, down from $91.2 million a year earlier.
"People are going to be focussing on comments from management on what has happened to their market share in Australia and New Zealand," Vaughan said.
There was hefty volume in Air New Zealand 'B' shares, which ended four cents stronger at $4.10, but Brierley topped the turnover with 3.96 million shares traded. BIL closed a cent weaker at $1.29.
Brokers said liquidity in the New Zealand share market remained subdued despite the Dow's 173-point surge overnight and falling domestic interest rates.
They said concerns that economic growth may still be slowing in New Zealand and could restrict company earnings had tinged the generally positive tone with an element of caution.
-- Matthew Brockett, Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 473-3736
